items.content_html:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Danna Hayes

Danna.hayes@maine.gov

Attorney General Frey, along with the Attorneys General of 47 other states and territories, announce preliminary approval of their plan to distribute funds to consumers following multiple settlements with drug manufacturers accused of conspiring to inflate prices of generic drugs.

AUGUSTA – Attorney General Frey is urging consumers to check their eligibility for compensation for certain generic drug purchases and to submit a claim for compensation. This month, the U.S. District Court for the District of Connecticut granted preliminary approval of a plan, filed by Maine and a coalition of 47 other states and territories, to distribute settlement funds paid by generic drug manufacturers in exchange for settlement of claims that those companies illegally conspired to raise the prices of generic drugs.

The coalition previously announced settlements with the manufacturers Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex, Heritage, and Heritage’s parent company, Emcure, totaling approximately $96.5 million. The multistate coalition’s distribution plan aims to return millions of dollars from those settlement funds to those potentially harmed by the elevated prices of the generic drugs that are the subjects of those settlements.

If you purchased a listed generic drug between May 2009 and December 2019, you may be eligible for compensation. To determine your eligibility, call 1-866-290-0182 (Toll-Free), email info@AGGenericDrugs.com or visit https://www.AGGenericDrugs.com. The deadline for submitting a claim is March 8, 2027.

Maine is part of a coalition of nearly all states and territories engaged in a series of antitrust cases, starting first in 2016. The first complaint included Heritage and 17 other corporate defendants, two individual defendants, and 15 generic drugs. The second complaint was filed in 2019 against Teva Pharmaceuticals and 21 of the nation’s largest generic drug manufacturers. The complaint names 16 individual senior executive defendants. The third complaint, to be tried first, focuses on 80 topical generic drugs that account for billions of dollars of sales in the United States and names 26 corporate defendants and 10 individual defendants. The States filed a fourth complaint earlier this year, alleging that Novartis AG, Sandoz Group AG and Sandoz AG, are liable for Sandoz’s alleged conduct and for fraudulently transferring assets. Seven pharmaceutical executives have been cooperating to support the States’ claims in these cases.

items.title: US Department of Labor cites Florida pipeline installation contractor for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards after March fatality
items.content_text: ORLANDO, FL – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an Orlando-based pipeline installation contractor for willfully exposing employees to safety hazards after an incident claimed the life of a worker at a New Smyrna Beach worksite in March 2026.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration found that on March 17, 2026, T & T Pipeline Co. Inc. employees were replacing a drill bit on a horizontal drilling machine when the pipe stem began to rotate and fatally struck the employee.OSHA cited the employer with a willful violation for exposing employees to struck-by hazards when working on a horizontal directional drilling machine and proposed $165,514 in penalties. The company has 15 business days from receipt of their citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Visit OSHA’s website for information on developing a workplace safety and health program. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

items.title: US Department of Labor cites New Jersey car wash for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards, proposes more than $446K in fines
items.content_text: SICKLERVILLE, NJ – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a New Jersey car wash service for willfully exposing workers to safety hazards related to hazardous energy and excessive noise levels, proposing $446,864 in penalties.The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration found that ModWash LLC, an express car wash service operating multiple locations throughout the country, including five in Sicklerville, willfully exposed workers to hazardous energy by failing to lock out equipment prior to conducting maintenance activities and not using energy control procedures. The agency also cited ModWash for two repeat violations for failing to have clear lockout procedures and specific instructions for controlling all energy sources and not training employees on equipment lockout/tagout processes. In addition, the employer was cited for five serious violations for failing to develop and implement a noise monitoring program, establish a baseline audiogram for employees within six months of exposure, train employees exposed to noise above 85 decibels, provide lockout/tagout devices, and attach such devices to machines prior to servicing them.The company has 15 business days from receipt of their citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website for information on developing a workplace safety and health program. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 21, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that began September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

 LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address. 
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

The Rooker-Feldman doctrine bars federal district courts from exercising

applies only to fnal judgments rendered by the highest court of a State 
in which a decision could be had, or whether it also bars suit when the 
state-court judgment at issue remains subject to further review in state 
appellate proceedings.

items.title: Berwick Solar, LLC v. Public Utilities Commission et al.
items.content_text:
MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT Reporter of Decisions 
Decision:  2026 ME 98 
Docket: PUC-25-51 
Argued: January 7, 2026 
Decided:  September 17, 2026 
 
Panel:  STANFILL, C.J., and MEAD, LAWRENCE, and DOUGLAS, JJ., and HORTON, A.R.J. 
 
 
BERWICK SOLAR, LLC 
 
v. 
 
PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION et al. 
 
 
LAWRENCE, J. 
[¶1]  Berwick Solar, LLC, appeals from an order of the Public Utilities 
Commission dismissing its complaint against Central Maine Power Company 
(CMP) alleging that CMP issued final reconciliation statements outside the time 
periods established in both 65-407 C.M.R. ch. 324, § 15(J) (effective Nov. 20, 
2023)1 and the standard-form Interconnection Agreement (IA) that Berwick 
Solar and CMP entered into under Chapter 324.  See 65-407 C.M.R. ch. 324, 
§ 4(A).  We affirm.    
 
1  As noted by the Commission in its briefing, none of the parties argue that anything besides the 
current version of Chapter 324 (effective Nov. 2023) should apply despite Berwick Solar and CMP 
entering the IA on March 6, 2020.  The Commission applied the current version in the order on appeal 
here.  Although the version of Chapter 324 provided by Berwick Solar in the appendix in this case 
was effective January 9, 2022, we cite the current version of Chapter 324.     
 2 
I.  BACKGROUND 
[¶2]  The following facts and procedural background are drawn from the 
administrative record and the Commission’s order dated January 15, 2025.  
See, e.g., Off. of the Pub. Advoc. v. Pub. Utils. Comm’n, 2023 ME 77, ¶ 2, 306 A.3d 
633. 
[¶3]  On March 6, 2020, Berwick Solar and CMP entered into the IA 
pursuant to 65-407 C.M.R. ch. 324, § 4(A), which provides the method by which 
small electric power generators may interconnect with electrical transmission

items.title: US Department of Labor investigation finds Chicago construction employer exposed workers to continued safety hazards, proposes $265K in penalties
items.content_text: CHICAGO – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Calumet City-based residential construction and carpentry employer after two separate investigations into its continued failure to provide fall protection for workers. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration investigated two worksites operated by Martin Araujo – doing business as Araujo Construction Corp. – and found that carpenters and general construction laborers were installing roof rafters and roof sheeting without fall protection, exposing them to falls of up to 25 feet. OSHA cited Araujo Construction with two willful violations for not providing fall protection, while working from heights during residential construction at the two worksites. OSHA also cited the employer with nine repeat safety violations for failing to provide head and eye protection, lacking handrails on stairways, and failing to make sure ladders extended three feet above access areas. Additionally, OSHA issued a serious violation to Araujo Construction for not having safe access to a platform, and an other-than-serious violation for lacking training certifications. OSHA proposed $265,868 in combined penalties.Martin Araujo has 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.  Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970, employers are responsible for providing safe and healthful workplaces for their employees. OSHA’s role is to ensure these conditions for America’s working men and women by setting and enforcing standards, and providing training, education and assistance. See OSHA’s website for more information.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 14, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that began September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address. 
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink. 

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access, training credit, and post-trainin

items.content_html:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Robert and Jackie Norton's son was waiting for them in California 25 years ago. He was about to get married, but his parents, a retired couple from Lubec, never made it to the ceremony. Their plane, American Airlines Flight 11, hit the North Tower of the World Trade Center in a horrific act of terrorism on September 11, 2001.

Katie Ward, the sister of Stephen Ward, said her brother couldn't wait to take over the big city when he moved to New York. A native of Gorham, Maine, Stephen had big plans, and he encouraged everyone to go after what they wanted and live their best lives. Stephen was working on the 101st floor of the North Tower at the World Trade Center that fateful day.

Robert Jalbert was raised in Lewiston and lived in Swampscott, Massachusetts, when he boarded United Flight 175 for a business trip to California. People described him as an easygoing guy, a good friend, and a proud father who went to church every Sunday and served as a Eucharistic Minister. His flight struck the South Tower of the World Trade Center.

Attorney Jim Roux of Portland, someone who loved hiking Mount Washington. He was also on United Flight 175. Through this Saturday, September 12th, the summit of Mount Washington will be lit by two pillars of light that will be visible from 100 miles away to honor Jim Roux and the thousands of others whose lives were cut short that day.

Commander Robert Schlegel was a devoted husband, a decorated officer, and an avid ice hockey and football player. Originally from Gray, Maine, Commander Schlegel had been awarded the Purple Heart and other medals for his career-long service in the U.S. Navy. He had been promoted just a month before he boarded American Airlines Flight 77, which was then flown into the Pentagon, killing all on board.

25 years ago, Maine and the nation were forever changed by the September 11th terrorist attacks. On this solemn anniversary, I join the Maine people in pausing to remember the nearly 3,000 souls taken from us that day, including the six beloved people from Maine. And in saluting the courageous first responders who rushed towards danger, including those heroes still living with devastating health conditions caused by exposure to toxic flames and fumes.

One of those firefighters moved to Falmouth, Maine. Kevin Hogan wasn't working on September 11, but when the first plane struck the World Trade Center, he jumped into a pickup truck, heading to Ground Zero. Through a storm of ash, he and other firefighters searched for scraps of clothing and under rubble, praying to find and return loved ones to their families. So today, we recognize first responders like Kevin, and we also thank the many servicemembers who stepped up to keep our nation safe then and in the years since.

And we thank our friends in other countries who stood by us. On September 11, more than 250 flights were forced to divert to Canada, including 38 commercial flights that touched down in Gander, Newfoundland, when more than 7,000 passengers were stranded. A local TV station put out a call to "lend a hand, do what you can," and residents opened their homes to Americans in need. Now, more than ever before, we should remember that kindness of our neighbors to the North. 

Although more than a hundred million Americans are too young to remember that dark day, today, we take a moment to remember and to honor those who perished that day, as well as the first responders who ran towards danger and stayed through the devastating aftermath, and the men and women who stepped up and who continue to step up to keep us safe.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and on behalf of the 1.4 million people of the state of Maine, we honor those who perished, those who helped, those who stood by us, 25 years ago, September 11, 2001.

If granted, the exemptions would enable these individuals who have had one or more seizures and are taking anti-seizure medication to operate CMVs in interstate commerce.

items.title: Hazardous Materials: Notice of Administrative Determination of Preemption for Common Law Tort Claims Concerning the Transportation of Gasoline
items.content_text: The Exxon Mobil Corporation (Exxon) seeks a determination that Federal law preempts State common law claims brought against it in New Jersey concerning the safe transportation of gasoline in commerce. PHMSA is issuing a final administrative determination concluding that the State common law tort claims presented by Exxon are preempted. Each of these duties, if imposed, would present an obstacle to compliance with the Federal regulatory framework essential for the safe transportation of gasoline. In addition, any claims about covered subjects, such as the marking, loading and unloading, and classification of gasoline that are not substantively the same as the applicable HMR provisions are preempted.

Temporary Changes to Referral and Authorization Processes Ending November 30, 2026

Sep 08, 2026

Beginning December 1, 2026, the Department will require members to complete a Single Assessment within the past 12 months before processing referrals, prior authorization requests, and continued stay reviews for children’s medium- and high-intensity services. 

As previously communicated, the Department temporarily reinstated direct-to-provider referral and prior authorization processes while operational challenges with the Single Assessment process were being addressed. That temporary process will end November 30, 2026. 

The Single Assessment process has stabilized significantly, with assessments now completed in an average of 7.5 business days after a request is submitted. 

Thank you for your continued partnership with the Single Assessment process.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 08, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that begins September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address. 
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink. 

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access
